column2: Rucz et al. (2021) do not name the wood of the Sonor Orff soprano bars beyond rosewood, and print no stiffness for the bars: only the blank's measured density (1116 kg/m3, SD 20, eight blanks) and its measured vertical modes (1040, 2728, 4976 Hz). The cards take E_L from the Wood Handbook Indian rosewood pack and the orthotropic ratios from the Wood Handbook Honduras mahogany pack. That is a declared stand-in, a choice, and two species mixed; it is not this specimen and no E_L was fitted to a frequency.
column3: unbounded for the species; the stand-in's own result at mesh rung 2 is that its vertical modes (756.5, 1921.9, 3400.5, 5027.7 Hz) fall 27.3, 29.5, 31.7 and 31.3 percent below Rucz's measured 1040, 2728, 4976 and 7320 Hz
column4: any claim that a render matches the Orff bar or any recorded xylophone or marimba bar; absolute pitch of the bar; the sign of every spectral comparison that depends on it
column5: Rucz et al. (stiffness or species of the bars), or a measured E_L, E_R, G set for the same bar stock

column2: The Wood Handbook rows are species means across many specimens at 12 percent moisture, not this specimen. The Rucz density row is measured on this stock at an unstated moisture, so the card combines a measured density with tabulated stiffness from other timber.
column3: not bounded: the packs used carry no within-species spread and the cards print none
column4: the uncertainty of every mode frequency, decay and line level; any claim of the form render equals measurement within a stated percent
column5: a measured E_L and density from one bar

column2: The bars of the real instrument carry a circular-arc undercut (125 mm grindstone, 6.8 to 8.2 mm thick at mid-bar, from Rucz Sec. III.A). The three-dimensional mode check against the printed A5 modes (check B, f2/f1 target 3.600, f3/f1 target 6.032, thresholds 5 and 10 percent) FAILED: at the largest printed thickness 8.2 mm the model gives 3.850 (+6.9 percent) and 7.008 (+16.2 percent), and at 6.8 mm it gives 4.337 (+20.5 percent) and 8.244 (+36.7 percent). The shape of the cut is therefore an unknown that the printed facts do not close. Rucz's own finite-element model of the real A5 bar misses its measured f3 by +9.1 percent, so part of the miss belongs to the source's own geometry description.
column3: check B failed at every printed mid-bar thickness; the uncut blank agrees with Rucz's finite-element blank modes within 0.55 percent (one-dimensional beam) and with the measured blank modes within 1.5 percent (three-dimensional solid at Rucz's own moduli, not at the stand-in)
column4: any cut-bar render, any marimba or xylophone note, the bar's overtone tuning, and the vibraphone and marimba families (no cited undercut exists for them); the two cards are the uncut blank only
column5: a printed profile or a measured thickness map of one real bar from the authors; the paper's supplementary material (a sensitivity study of material parameters) was not read

column2: Rucz print the resonator opening's area (46.32 cm2 for resonator 6) and say it is rectangular with rounded corners at the centre of the top plate, covered by two bars, but print neither its dimensions nor the overlap of the bar. The card puts the wet interval at 0.10 to 0.17 m along the bar across its full width (21.7 cm2 of the 46.32 cm2 opening). That interval is declared, not measured.
column3: unbounded; the wet fraction is 47 percent of the printed opening, and the coupled line level scales with the wet area, so the resonator line has no stated bound
column4: the level and the lifetime of the resonator line against the bar fundamental; any claim of the resonator gain
column5: the opening dimensions and bar overlap from the authors, or a drawing of the box

column2: The lumped Helmholtz element built from the printed volume, opening area and 3 mm neck misses the measured resonance of the six resonators in Rucz Table III: +1.7, -3.4, -4.3, -7.4, -7.5 and -11.0 percent (the element minus the measurement, resonator 1 to 6). These are reported as measured; the card does not trim the neck to hit the measured value. The resonator over which the card is placed (resonator 6) is the -11 percent one.
column3: +1.7 to -11 percent in resonance frequency across the six printed resonators
column4: the resonator line's frequency against the measured 1007.5 Hz; any claim that the resonator is tuned to the bar
column5: the end-correction and box-wall compliance model for a thin-neck box opening (Rucz Sec. III.C names a very short neck), or the authors' measured effective length

column2: The coupled render leaves out the box walls, the neighbouring bars' screening of the opening, and the bar supports. Rucz's measured detuning of the resonance by the bars is 6 to 15 percent (Table IV) and is not reproduced. The neck radiation is a compact flanged monopole at the opening, not a resolved box.
column3: not estimated; the detuning range from the source is 6 to 15 percent in resonance frequency, and no bound on level is printed
column4: any level comparison with a recording of a resonated bar; any claim of the radiated field in the box's near field
column5: a resolved box model with the bar rows over the opening, checked against Rucz Table IV
